criterion: leakage-resistant dataset layer: provenance, checksums, label audit, URL-quality audit, exact/canonical dedup, domain-disjoint split, strict + natural external views, compatibility gate
numerical_evidence: Gram 799,565 / Phresh 666,300 rows after cleaning; strict external n = 126,116 (G->P) / 118,390 (P->G); contamination removed from natural view 24.96% / 1.29%; P0 gate 21/21; 238/238 sanity checks
interpretation: the evaluation substrate is auditable and domain-unseen; supports Contribution 1

criterion: domain-invariant block: max normalised Wasserstein <= 0.15 and block domain-classifier AUC <= 0.60 (pinned Phase-1 gate)
numerical_evidence: F69-R-v3 = F54-R (54) + 15 domain-invariant = 69 features; max W = 0.1341 (<= 0.15); block domain AUC 0.6757 -> 0.5501 (target <= 0.60); promoted
interpretation: the selected feature block has substantially reduced domain-identifying signal; this does NOT make the corpora identical (full-representation origin AUC stays high)

criterion: strict-external ROC-AUC >= 0.80 for at least one zero-shot/UDA model in BOTH directions (pinned Gate 2; changelog: tightened any->both in rev 7)
interpretation: UDA (unlabeled target TRAIN + word expert/fusion + self-training, no target VAL/TEST labels) materially improves cross-corpus ranking in both directions

criterion: best semi-supervised multi-source strict-external ACCURACY >= 0.95 in BOTH directions (pinned Gate 3)
numerical_evidence: G->P best 0.9438 (M2h multi-source hybrid (target-val tuned), n=126,116) vs 0.95; P->G best 0.9558 (M2s multi-source stacked text (target-val tuned), n=118,390)
interpretation: one direction narrowly misses 95%; this is a semi-supervised target-adaptation benchmark (uses target TRAIN labels + target VAL selection), NOT a zero-shot/UDA claim
paper_role: secondary supporting result, reported as near-threshold

criterion: P3 AND P5/P6/P7 prediction-flip rate <= 15% for at least one repaired variant (pinned Gate 4)
numerical_evidence: P3 dot-segment max flip: 57.45% baseline -> 56.90% augmented -> 40.25% revision-7 repaired (never <= 15%); P5/P6/P7 max flip: 55.80% baseline -> 14.95% augmented (within 15%)
interpretation: P5/P6/P7 are repairable; P3 is a persistent raw-representation sensitivity. RFC 3986 canonicalisation neutralises P3 mechanically (~0% flip) but degenerates the ERS reliability target (y_rel constant), so it is NOT enabled globally; P3 is retained as an honest limitation

criterion: cross-family rho(E0, y_rel) > 0.10 on >= 3 of 4 runs (pinned Phase-5 gate)
numerical_evidence: rho(E0, y_rel) by run: gram|F48=0.3563, gram|F69-R-v3=0.3605, phresh|F48=0.2907, phresh|F69-R-v3=0.0691
interpretation: the redesigned non-circular target (0.5*held-out challenge stability + 0.5*calibration-family stability, P1/P2 removed) is learnable on most but not all run configurations; the failing configuration (phresh|F69-R-v3) is reported, not hidden
paper_role: methodological result, mixed and reported honestly

criterion: ERS predicts held-out explanation stability: Spearman(ERS, S_challenge) > 0 with Holm-adjusted p < alpha
numerical_evidence: test rho: gram|F48=+0.3715, gram|F69-R-v3=+0.4232, phresh|F48=+0.5100, phresh|F69-R-v3=+0.1861; external rho: gram|F48=+0.3212, gram|F69-R-v3=+0.3697, phresh|F48=+0.4489, phresh|F69-R-v3=+0.3052; all Holm-significant; ERS beats confidence on 4/4 external runs
interpretation: ERS carries information about explanation stability, and is the stronger predictor of held-out explanation stability on the evaluated external runs (confidence is stronger in-domain on 2 of 4 runs)

criterion: ERS carries information beyond confidence about correctness: LRT (Error ~ C vs Error ~ C + ERS + CxERS) Holm-adjusted p < alpha on the in-domain test sample
numerical_evidence: LRT p_holm: gram|F69-R-v3 LRT=6.815, p_holm=0.363, phresh|F69-R-v3 LRT=0.345, p_holm=1
interpretation: ERS did not provide statistically supported incremental information about classification correctness beyond calibrated confidence under the preregistered model; external associations exist but track the reliability/correctness divergence (reversal), not decision value
paper_role: central negative result (defines the paper's framing)

criterion: DTS AURC < confidence AURC with the 95% paired-bootstrap CI of the difference entirely below 0 on EVERY external run (all-pairs, never any-pair)
numerical_evidence: 0/12 external DTS cells beat confidence with CI excluding 0; gram|F69-R-v3 conf AURC 0.20714 vs DTS 0.21166; phresh|F69-R-v3 conf 0.25889 vs DTS 0.26423
interpretation: calibrated confidence remained the stronger signal for selective classification risk in the evaluated external settings; the gate was not loosened and the negative result is kept
paper_role: central negative result (defines the paper's framing)

criterion: report calibration behaviour under temporal shift (pre-registered supporting analysis; PhreshPhish temporal slices, date never a feature)
numerical_evidence: gram|F69-R-v3 strict-external: ECE 0.0716 (2025Q3) -> 0.2497 (2025Q4) while ROC-AUC 0.7630 -> 0.7696; phishing prevalence 14.4% -> 57.0% (confound: prevalence shift)
interpretation: calibration deteriorates substantially under temporal shift while ranking is stable; only two adequately-powered quarters exist, so this is directional evidence
paper_role: supporting result (motivates recalibration under deployment shift)

criterion: external ROC-AUC (F54-R) > external ROC-AUC (F48) with a DeLong 95% CI excluding 0 (pre-registered)
interpretation: resolved at paper lock from the executed paired DeLong comparison (the Section-48 'unavailable' was a lookup bug): representation repair does NOT improve strict-external transfer; both CIs exclude zero in the negative direction
paper_role: negative result, now evaluable and reported

criterion: checksums, split integrity, no target-TEST labels in any fit/tune/calibrate/threshold step, 238 sanity checks, manifest
numerical_evidence: 238/238 executed sanity checks passed; dataset SHA-256 verified against the recorded provenance audit; seed 42; manifest revision 11
interpretation: the executed run is fully auditable; paper-lock outputs document which results are reused versus recomputed
